verses.1: And he began to speak to them in parables. A man named Ambelus was born. He built a shelter and a tower, and let the farmers live there. Then he abandoned them.
verses.2: And at that time, a slave was sent to the farmers, so that he could collect the fruits of the olive trees from them.
verses.3: And after taking him away, they left him there empty-handed.
verses.4: And once again, another slave was sent to them. They also beheaded and mutilated that slave as well.
verses.5: And he sent another one along; they also were killed. Many others were also killed, some by being burned, and others by being executed.
verses.6: He still had one more son, a beloved child. He sent him to them at the last moment, saying that they should take my son away from me.
verses.7: But those farmers said to themselves, “He is indeed the heir. Let us kill him, then, and his inheritance will belong to us.”
verses.8: And when they took it, they burned it. They also threw it out of the amphora.
verses.9: What will the master of the vineyard do? He will harvest and sell the grapes, and give them to others instead.
verses.10: And you also did not read this writing. That stone, which the builders rejected, became the head of the gordon.
verses.11: It happened because of the Lord. Is it truly amazing to us?
verses.12: They also wanted to keep him safe. They were afraid of the crowd, as they knew that he had said those jokes in order to mock them. So, they abandoned him and left.
verses.13: And they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to try to persuade him to stop farming.
verses.14: And they come and say to him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and not deceitful. You do not look at people’s faces; instead, you truly teach the way of God. Is it right or wrong to give Caesar a reward? Should we give it or not?”
verses.15: But he, knowing their manner of speaking, said to them, “What are you troubling me with? Give me some money so that I can see.”
verses.16: And those who were sealed said to them, “What is this image and what is this symbol?” They replied, “A king.”
verses.17: But Jesus said to them, “What the Emperor gives to Caesar, the Lord gives to the Lord.” And they marveled at this.
verses.18: And the Sadducees come to him, saying that there is no resurrection. They also ask him questions about this.
verses.19: Teacher Moses said to us that if a brother dies and leaves no wife, and no children, then his brother should take his wife and restore his lineage to his brother.
verses.20: He had seven brothers. The first one married a woman, but after he died, he did not produce any offspring.
verses.21: And the second one also took her. He died without leaving behind any semen. And the third one did the same.
verses.22: And the seven also did not produce any offspring. In fact, the woman died as well.
verses.23: In this transformation, when someone transforms into a woman, who will be their wife? After all, there are seven women who can become their wives.
verses.24: Jesus said to them, “Don’t be deceived by this; don’t ignore the writings and the power of God.”
verses.25: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are married. Instead, they are like angels in heaven.
verses.26: As for the dead, you do not know what Moses said to them in the Book about those who die. What did God say to them? “I am God Abraham’s God, and I am also God Isaac’s God, and I am God Jacob’s God.”
verses.27: There is no god of the dead, but of the living. Be very careful not to be deceived.
verses.28: And when he went up to one of the officials and heard them discussing something, realizing that his words had been well received, he asked him: “What is the first commandment of all?”
verses.29: Jesus said that He was the First. “Hear, Israel! The Lord our God is one.”
verses.30: And you will love your Lord God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.
verses.31: The second one is: “Love your neighbor as yourself.” There’s no greater command than this.
verses.32: And the clerk said to him, “Well, teacher, you truly said that there is one person, and no other person besides him.”
verses.33: And to love him wholeheartedly, with all one’s strength and devotion, is indeed the most important of all acts of love and sacrifice.
verses.34: And when Jesus saw that he was thinking deeply, he said to him, “You will not be far from the kingdom of God.” And no one will ever force him to do anything against his will.
verses.35: And when Jesus spoke, he taught in the temple. How can the scribes say that Christ is the son of David?
verses.36: David said in that holy spirit, “Lord, my Lord!” He sat to the right of me, until I could defeat your enemies under your feet.
verses.37: David said to him, “Lord, where does he come from?” And the crowd listened to him with pleasure.
verses.38: And in his teachings, he said: “See how those officials walk around in their uniforms, and how they act during auctions.”
verses.39: and as the first bishop at gatherings, and as the first clistian at meals.
verses.40: Those who destroyed the homes of others and prayed for a long time in prayer… they will suffer even more punishment.
verses.41: And he sat down opposite the bronze basin, and observed how the crowd poured lead into that basin. Many wealthy people also poured a lot of lead into it.
verses.42: And when a poor woman came along, she gave two coins. Those coins were used as payment for the service.
verses.43: And when he called his disciples together, he said to them, “I tell you that that poor woman put more of her offerings into the basket than anyone else did.”
verses.44: For they all gave him what they had extra; she, on the other hand, gave away everything she had from her own savings. She gave away everything she owned during her entire life.
